note: Curated by hand. A ticker that is not in the selected B3 universe is dropped by the build and counted, never invented.

themes.label: BANKS & FINANCIALS
themes.note: The private and state banks, the exchange and the payment/fintech names. Net interest margin and the provisioning cycle drive earnings; these carry a P/E and a P/B but no free cash flow.

themes.label: OIL, GAS & FUELS
themes.note: Petrobras and the independent producers, plus the fuel distribution and sugar/ethanol names. Crude, the pre-salt cycle and the government's pricing policy are the swing factors.

themes.label: MINING & STEEL
themes.note: Iron ore, pellets, steel and the metals chain. Vale is the global iron-ore benchmark; the steelmakers read Chinese demand and the BRL cost base.

themes.label: AGRIBUSINESS & PROTEIN
themes.note: Soy, corn, sugar, coffee, orange and the protein exporters. A weaker BRL helps the export margin; weather and Chinese demand set the cycle.

themes.label: PULP, PAPER & PACKAGING
themes.note: Eucalyptus pulp and paper. Pulp is a dollar price with a BRL cost base, so the exchange rate is half the story.

themes.label: CONSUMER & RETAIL
themes.note: Beer, food, fashion, e-commerce and the retailers. Domestic demand, real income and the Selic rate drive the cycle.

themes.label: UTILITIES & SANITATION
themes.note: Electricity, transmission, water and gas. Regulated returns, the hydrological cycle and the renewal of concessions are the drivers.

themes.label: INDUSTRIALS & CAPITAL GOODS
themes.note: Motors, auto parts, machinery and electrical equipment. The read is investment, credit and the BRL cost of imported components.

themes.label: LOGISTICS & TRANSPORT
themes.note: Rail, ports, toll roads and the trucking/rental names. Volumes track the commodity and industrial cycle; concessions and leverage are the risk.

themes.label: HEALTHCARE
themes.note: Hospitals, diagnostics, pharmacies and the health insurers. A domestic, defensive sector with a long runway and little commodity exposure.

themes.label: PROPERTY & CONSTRUCTION
themes.note: Developers and construction. Presales, inventory, mortgage rates and the Selic rate are the read; the balance sheet is the story, so P/B matters.

themes.label: TELECOM & TECHNOLOGY
themes.note: The incumbent telecom, enterprise software, e-commerce infrastructure and the digital names. Cash flow and growth, not commodities.

themes.label: SIGNIFICANT BDRs
themes.note: The curated B3 BDR lens: Nu Holdings, XP, Inter, MercadoLibre, StoneCo, PagSeguro, VTEX, Globant, JBS N.V., Aura, Brazil Potash and Eve, plus the global mega-caps. BDRs are depositary receipts of foreign companies; the cap is the global company cap in BRL, the price is the BDR line, and the ratios are company-level in the underlying report currency. They are excluded from the 303 domestic totals.
